messages.text: Me and my wife have three kids. I get paid every two weeks. Do we qualify for SNAP or TennCare?

Happy to help you check. I have a few questions first.

1. How old are your three kids? And is anyone in the family pregnant, or does anyone have a disability?
2. How much do you get paid each time (before taxes)? Does your wife have any income?
Kids are 10, 6, and 3. Nobody's pregnant or has a disability that I know of. I get $1,600 every two weeks before taxes. My wife doesn't have any income.

Thanks, that helps. I need a few more details to run the check.

1. About how old are you and your wife?
2. How much do you pay each month for rent or mortgage? Do you pay for heating or cooling separately, or other utilities like electric or water?

I'm 36 and my wife is 34. Rent is $1,200 a month and we pay heating/cooling on top of that. I don't think we have any other bills, so no electric or water on our end, I think it's included. Is that enough or do you need anything else?

Almost. I need three more answers, and then I can give you the full picture.

1. Do you pay for child care so you or your wife can work or go to school? If so, about how much a month?
2. Does anyone in the family already get food assistance (SNAP), WIC, or TennCare?
3. This one is optional. About how much do you have in cash and bank accounts combined? SNAP has a savings limit.
Child care: no, we don't pay for any. Food help: nobody in the family gets SNAP, WIC, or TennCare right now. Savings: about $300 total, cash and checking together.

Your family looks likely to qualify for food assistance (SNAP) and for TennCare for your kids. WIC also looks likely for your 3-year-old. Only the state agencies decide, so this is a first check, not a decision.

## Food assistance (SNAP): likely
- **Estimated benefit: about $614 a month.** This is an estimate. The agency sets the real amount.
- Your income before taxes is about $3,440 a month. That is your $1,600 every two weeks, converted to a monthly amount. For a family of 5, the limit is $4,191 before deductions and $3,224 after them. After deductions, your income is about $2,007.
- Your rent and heating or cooling costs lower your countable income. So does 20% of your pay.
- Your $300 in savings is well under the $3,000 limit for cash and bank accounts.
- **Apply:** [OneDHS portal](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp?id=start_snap_application) or call 866-311-4287.
- Sources: USDA's [FY 2027 limits and deductions](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap/allotment/cola), [7 CFR 273.10](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-273.10), and the [USDA SNAP state directory](https://www.fns.usda.gov/snap-directory-entry/tennessee).
- The tool used the latest published utility allowance figures, which ran through Sept. 30, 2026. Newer ones weren't available, so the amount could shift a little.

## TennCare / CoverKids
- **Your 3 kids: likely.**
  - Your 10-year-old and 6-year-old are within the limit of $4,288 a month for a family of 5.
  - Your 3-year-old is within the limit of $4,578.
- **You and your wife: unlikely.** For parents, the limit is $3,224 a month, and your income is $3,440. You can still apply.
- **Apply:** [TennCare Connect](https://tenncareconnect.tn.gov/) or call 855-259-0701.
- Source: the Division of TennCare's [Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/coverkids/coverkids/redirect-income-guidelines.html).
- TennCare uses tax-based income. The tool used your gross income as a stand-in, so the agency's numbers may differ.

## WIC: likely, for your 3-year-old
- WIC serves children under 5. Your income of $3,440 is under the limit of $5,964 a month for 5 people.
- The clinic will also do a short health and nutrition check.
- **Apply:** your local health department clinic, or call 1-800-DIAL-WIC (1-800-342-5942). More at [tn.gov/health/wic](https://www.tn.gov/health/wic.html).
- Sources: USDA's [WIC income guidelines](https://www.fns.usda.gov/wic/fr-042926) and [7 CFR 246.2](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-7/section-246.2).

## Help applying
Dial **211** for free local help.

Report your income and household accurately on each application. That protects you, because overpayments have to be paid back.
